**Answer:** One of the most iconic and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Statue of Liberty”** (officially *Liberty Enlightening the World*), completed in 1886. **Why it’s considered the most famous:** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi (French sculptor) | | **Completion Year** | 1886 | | **Location** | New York Harbor, United States | | **Cultural Impact** | • Symbol of freedom and democracy worldwide.
• Frequently used as a backdrop in films, news broadcasts, and popular media.
• Recognized by millions of tourists each year. | | **Technical Highlights** | • Constructed using a copper exterior over an iron framework.
• Designed to withstand harsh marine conditions. | | **Legacy** | • Became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
• Inspired countless replicas and artistic references across the globe. | While other 19th‑century masterpieces—such as Auguste Rodin’s *The Kiss* (1889) or *The Gates of Hell* (unfinished, 1880s)—are highly celebrated within art circles, *The Statue of Liberty* stands out as the most universally recognized sculpture from that era, both culturally and historically.
